Kuali Basics
Kuali Basics
Quick Links

Kuali Curriculum Management (CM) is URI’s system for managing university curriculum and the curriculum approval process. It uses electronic forms and workflow to route course, program, and specialization proposals through the appropriate levels of review and approval.

Kuali serves as the central source for approved curriculum information:
Kuali CM — Manages curriculum proposals and the approval workflow.
Academic Catalog — Pulls approved course, program, and specialization information from Kuali.
eCampus — Receives approved course information from Kuali for implementation in future terms.

Information entered into Kuali can flow directly into the official academic catalog and eCampus. Proposals should therefore be clear, accurate, and unambiguous, as the information entered during the proposal process becomes part of the University’s official curriculum.
Access to Kuali CM is limited to faculty, Deans, and select administrators and staff. Only faculty members may submit curriculum proposals.

Faculty members automatically have access to Kuali CM, as faculty are the users authorized to submit curricular proposals. If this is your first time accessing Kuali CM, sign in using your URI Microsoft 365 account.

Access to Kuali CM is also available to deans and select administrators or staff. In specific cases, other non-faculty users may request access.
Use the Kuali Access Package to request access using your URI SSO. After selecting Continue, you will be asked to provide your job or position title and a business justification for needing access. Once your request has been reviewed, you will be notified whether access has been granted.

Sign in to your Microsoft 365 Apps using your URI SSO.
Select Kuali Course Management from your application collection.
Alternatively, use the direct link to Kuali CM and bookmark it for future access.
Once logged in, select the Curriculum tile. This is where you can view current courses, programs, and specializations and, for authorized users, create proposals for new or modified curriculum.
When you enter Curriculum Management, the Dashboard serves as your homepage. It provides quick access to your proposals and items requiring your action.

My Proposals allows you to:
Continue working on Drafts you have started but not yet submitted.
View submitted proposals and their current workflow status.
Access proposals directly from the Dashboard.
Any proposals you begin but have not yet submitted will appear as Drafts. From this section, you can continue editing or delete a draft.
Select View All to see your complete list of proposals. The list can be filtered, downloaded, and printed.

My Action List displays your ten most recent items requiring action. These may include proposals that require you to:
Review and approve
Acknowledge
Edit and return to the workflow after being sent back by a reviewing committee
Use the navigation bar on the left side of the screen to access courses, programs, specializations, and proposals, including drafts, proposals under review, and approved records.

Use the search bar at the top of the Courses, Programs, Specializations, or Proposals pages to locate specific records. Use the filters on the right side of the page to narrow your results.
Status: Select Active when searching for current curricular items. Retired and Inactive statuses are not consistently used in Kuali CM.
Groups: Use Groups to locate curricular records associated with a specific department or college.

Kuali uses colored bars to indicate which version of a curricular record you are viewing.
🟢 Current Version — The version currently in effect. For most records, the earliest version available in Kuali is Fall 2022, when URI began using Kuali. Earlier historical versions are available in eCampus.
⚪ Past Version — An earlier version of the record, including inactive records.
🟣 Future Version — A version scheduled to become active in a future term.
↕️ Use the arrows next to the term dates to expand the record history and select an earlier or future version.

The status indicators below apply only when you are viewing a proposal and not the curricular record itself. The colored bar at the top of a proposal indicates where the proposal is in the curriculum approval workflow.
🟡 Draft — A new proposal or proposed change that has been created but not yet submitted to the workflow. Drafts can be edited or deleted.
🔵 Under Review — A proposal that has been submitted to the workflow and is currently moving through the approval process.
⚫ Denied — A proposal that has been denied during the review process. Denied proposals cannot be edited or resubmitted.
🟢 Approved — A proposal that has completed the required approval process and has been approved.
Tip: When viewing an approved proposal, you can switch to the current curricular record by selecting “View Active Course (Program / Specialization).”

Instructional Delivery Method
Tags: courses
Short Description: The instructional delivery method. Also known as "method of instruction.”
Instructional Delivery Method
Provided below is the complete list of approved methods of instruction, as proposed in FSEC Report #2024-2025-03 and subsequently approved by the Faculty Senate through Bill #24-25-12 on January 23, 2025.
A course in which the primary method is presentation and students are expected to participate in a variety of ways, such as small-group discussions, questions and answers, writing-exercises, etc.
Applied course work, generally involving experimentation or observation, typically using special equipment (including computers and specialized software).
Separate sections of a lecture course regularly scheduled for discussion.
Supervised work with an emphasis on performance and creativity in which faculty instruct, assist, and critique.
Course offered to a small group (usually no more than 20 students) where participants actively exchange ideas and findings based on readings or research.

One-on-one instruction in which the student enters into an agreement with the instructor that defines the focus of inquiry and nature of activities. Includes tutorials, directed readings, special projects.
Structured experiences where the primary aim is to connect theory with practice. Includes clinics, internships, externships, student teaching, field experiences. May include regular class meetings.
Similar to a seminar, with emphasis on applied rather than theoretical learning, but not offered for degree-program credit.

From your browser, navigate to Kuali Curriculum Management (CM).

From the left-hand navigation menu, select Programs.

The following sections of this walkthrough are grouped by section of the proposal form.
Select the applicable changes in the checkboxes/radio buttons.

Complete the following fields with your contact information.
Proposer Name Your name is automatically populated based on your Kuali account.
Proposer Title Enter your university role.
Proposer Email Enter your URI email address. This is the email reviewers will use if they have questions about your proposal.
Additional Proposer(s) Use this section to identify additional individuals who can speak to the proposed program.
Individuals listed here will not receive Kuali notifications or have access to edit the proposal. Their inclusion simply provides transparency to the reviewing committees about who else is involved in or can speak to the proposal.

Effective Term & Year Select the term and year in which you intend the program to become effective. If the selected effective term has passed the applicable deadline by the time the proposal reaches the Faculty Senate, it will automatically be updated to the next available term.
First Graduation Term with Modifications Select the term and year in which you anticipate the students will graduate with the changes proposed.
Credential Type This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Level This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Academic Calendar This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
Important Information about Changing a Program’s Academic Calendar
If a program is currently offered on the Traditional Academic Calendar and you would like to move it to the Accelerated Academic Calendar, you cannot simply change the calendar while students are still enrolled in the program. The existing program must first be fully taught out. This requires a proposal to suspend admission to the program. Once there are no students remaining in the program, the program can be moved from one academic calendar to the other.

Alternatively, you may propose a new program by cloning the existing program. This approach does not require Board of Trustees approval and is treated as a program modification. Creating a separate program allows students to be appropriately coded according to the academic calendar in which their program is offered (Traditional or Accelerated).
Program Locations Select all locations where the program will be offered.
College This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification Section of the proposal.
Department This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is unless you’ve selected Change Academic Home (department / college) from the Program Modification section of the proposal.
CIP Code This field will already be populated.
If it is not populated, enter the program’s current CIP Code as listed on eCampus.
If you are changing the program’s CIP code, make sure Change CIP Code is selected from the Program Modification section of the proposal, and enter the new code in the space provided.

🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is chosen for Is this interdisciplinary?
Additional Department(s) and College(s) Enter departments sharing ownership of this program.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Degree or Major is chosen for Credential Type.
Degree This field will already be populated. Leave the selection as is.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Major is chosen for Credential Type.

See Admission Requirements for criteria
Related toolkit entry: Admission Requirements
Total program credits Enter the total number of credits required to earn the credential.

Total core course credits Enter the total number of credits required for core courses.
Total elective course credits Enter the total number of credits required for elective courses.
🔽 The following field will appear only if Level is Undergraduate or Dual.
Total general education course credits Enter the total number of required General Education credits.
List the name(s) and title(s) of the individual(s) responsible for administering the program. Enter the name of the program director, department chair, or other individual responsible for administering the program.

🔽 This section will appear only if one of the options under Change Program Modality is chosen from the Program Modification section.
Are all required resources (faculty, staff, instructional equipment, etc.) currently available for this program? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following field will appear only if No is selected for the question above.
Describe the additional resources needed and provide a rationale.
Will the change in program modality offer any new assistantships, scholarships, and/or fellowships? Select Yes or No.
🔽 The following fields will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
List any new available assistantships, scholarships and/or fellowships.
Supporting Documentation Optional.
Describe how program resources, equipment, and technology comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state disability statutes.
For the proposed modality change, provide the number of currently enrolled students and explain how the change will impact their ability to complete the program and how they will be supported throughout the transition.
Will this change require additional funding, resources, or personnel?

🔽 The following field will appear only if Yes is selected for the question above.
Describe the anticipated additional funding, resources, or personnel required to support this modality change.
Attach supporting documentation Optional.

Once you have finalized your proposal draft:
Select Leave Edit Mode in the upper-right corner of the screen, just below the orange bar.

Your proposal will automatically be sent to the appropriate review committees. You may be contacted within Kuali Comments by the committees with questions to the proposal (an email will notify you automatically). You can also return to your proposal from your dashboard at any time to view the workflow status.

Grand Challenge
Tags: courses
Short Description: A General Education overlay centered on a complex contemporary issue and designed to engage students through interdisciplinary perspectives and ethical inquiry.
Grand Challenge
A Grand Challenge course centers on a complex issue of contemporary significance and provides students with opportunities to explore, question, and critically engage with the issue. The course incorporates at least two disciplinary perspectives and helps students make interdisciplinary connections through assignments, activities, and/or experiences. It also addresses the ethical challenges associated with the issue, providing students with opportunities to apply ethical concepts or frameworks in evaluating potential actions and their ramifications.
Proposers will complete the Grand Challenge section in their Kuali Course Proposal. This Grand Challenge Template is available as a resource to help prepare responses for submission.
